definitions.explanation: A type of graph that displays data points connected by straight line segments. Used to show changes over time or trends.

examples.japanese: {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフを{描|か}く。
{気温|きおん}の{変化|へんか}を{折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフで{表|あらわ}す。
examples.english: To show temperature changes with a line graph.

examples.japanese: この{折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフを{見|み}ると、{売|う}り{上|あ}げが{右肩上|みぎかたあ}がりに{伸|の}びているのがわかる。
examples.english: Looking at this line graph, you can see that sales have been steadily increasing.

notes:
Composed of {折|お}れ{線|せん} (broken line / polyline) + グラフ (graph). The name comes from the zigzag shape formed when data points are connected by straight lines.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフを{描|か}く: to draw a line graph
- {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフで{表|あらわ}す: to represent with a line graph
- {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフを{読|よ}み{取|と}る: to read/interpret a line graph

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {棒|ぼう}グラフ: bar graph — uses rectangular bars to represent data
- {円|えん}グラフ: pie chart — uses a circle divided into sectors
- {帯|おび}グラフ: band graph / stacked bar chart

NOTE:
Line graphs are taught in Japanese elementary school math ({算数|さんすう}) and are one of the basic graph types students learn alongside bar graphs and pie charts.
